claims.claim: Mistral 7B outperforms the best open 13B model (Llama 2) on all evaluated benchmarks, and Llama 1 34B in reasoning, mathematics and code
claims.quote: Mistral 7B outperforms the best open 13B model (Llama 2) across all evaluated benchmarks, and the best released 34B model (Llama 1) in reasoning, mathematics, and code generation.

claims.claim: Uses grouped-query attention (GQA) for faster inference and lower decoding memory
claims.quote: GQA significantly accelerates the inference speed, and also reduces the memory requirement during decoding, allowing for higher batch sizes hence higher throughput

claims.claim: Uses sliding window attention (SWA) to handle sequences of arbitrary length at reduced inference cost
claims.quote: coupled with sliding window attention (SWA) to effectively handle sequences of arbitrary length with a reduced inference cost.

claims.claim: Instruction-tuned model Mistral 7B – Instruct surpasses Llama 2 13B – Chat on human and automated benchmarks
claims.quote: We also provide a model fine-tuned to follow instructions, Mistral 7B – Instruct, that surpasses Llama 2 13B – chat model both on human and automated benchmarks.

claims.claim: Models released under Apache 2.0 with reference implementation for easy deployment
claims.quote: Mistral 7B is released under the Apache 2.0 license. This release is accompanied by a reference implementation1 facilitating easy deployment either locally or on cloud platforms

rerun.quote: We compare Mistral 7B to Llama, and re-run all benchmarks with our own evaluation pipeline for fair comparison.

scores_copied.quote: All models were re-evaluated on all metrics with our evaluation pipeline for accurate comparison.

third_party.quote: independent human evaluation was conducted on

coding.note: I coded the SWA ablation as NO. The paper does report a 2x speed gain over a vanilla attention baseline (p.2), but that only measures the kernel's speed. It is not a with/without comparison of trained models, so I took the lower level over PARTIAL. GQA has no comparison at all. Seeds are NR: the MT Bench ± std is over 10 evaluation iterations (p.5), not over independent training runs. I treated the 'Mistral system prompt' and 'self-reflection' prompting as uses of the model, not renames. The rolling buffer cache and pre-fill chunking appear in Section 2 but not in the abstract or introduction, so I left them out of the claims. The chat-model scores in Table 3 (ELO and MT Bench) have no stated source. The main base-model table was re-evaluated by the authors.
